run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:54:23Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is driven by ERROR-status spans recorded by frontend-proxy on its 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' operations (0.448/s ERROR vs 25.31/s UNSET in the 5-minute rate at 2026-11-18T00:00:00Z). Two components are visible: (a) sparse isolated error spans across the window (0-0.0333/s against ~14-15/s total ingress; a sampled 503 at 23:37:56Z whose child egress span has http.status_code=0), and (b) a concentrated burst at 23:56:00-23:57:00Z (78 then 42 ingress error spans per minute) that traces through checkout's client spans oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (44 errors each in the window ending 23:57:00Z) up to frontend's POST /api/checkout (74 then 44 error spans). At the same time the payment Deployment was rolled out: its pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:54:40Z with an unchanged image tag (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, revision 2); the old payment pod was killed at 23:54:43Z, the new container's gRPC server only logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 23:55:54.877Z and served its first charge at 23:56:32.929Z, and payment served zero charge spans in the windows ending 23:56:00Z and 23:57:00Z. The flagd ConfigMap currently holds a switched-on fault setting, paymentFailure defaultVariant '100%' ('Fail payment service charge requests n%', state ENABLED), while every other flag is 'off'; payment is the service that was restarted with an unchanged pod template, and no other object is seen applying a fault to it. Remaining uncertainty: payment itself never emitted an ERROR-status span and every charge it served logged 'Transaction complete.', the declared charge-failure fault was not observed directly, the moment paymentFailure was changed cannot be determined, and the cause of the sparse pre/post burst 503s is not established - hence conclusion partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy emitted ERROR-status spans: the 5-minute rate at 2026-11-18T00:00:00Z is 0.448/s STATUS_CODE_ERROR against 25.31/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET for service_name="frontend-proxy".

frontend-proxy's error spans are carried only by span_name "ingress" and span_name "router frontend egress": per-minute increases are 78 ingress / 78 egress in the window ending 23:56:00Z and 42 / 40 in the window ending 23:57:00Z, versus 0 or 2 in the surrounding minutes.

Before the burst the frontend-proxy ingress error rate was 0 to 0.0333/s against 14-15 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans/s (samples 23:32:00Z-23:45:00Z), i.e. isolated error spans already existed; at 2026-11-18T00:10:00Z the ingress error rate is 0.0077/s against 5.53/s UNSET, so sparse error spans persist after the burst.

A sampled failing trace at 23:37:56Z shows frontend-proxy operation "ingress" with status_tags error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR (749.9 ms) whose child span "router frontend egress" (same service) has error="true" and http.status_code=0, i.e. no upstream response; the parent load-generator GET returned 503.

checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (status STATUS_CODE_ERROR) and its server span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (STATUS_CODE_ERROR) each increased by 44 in the 60-second window ending 23:57:00Z, and were 0 in the adjacent windows.

payment service emits operations "charge" (internal) and "grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" (server); their 60-second increases were 76 at 23:55:00Z and then 0 in the windows ending 23:56:00Z and 23:57:00Z, resuming at 58.7 and 60 in the following windows.

Logs of the new payment pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht show no charge activity between container start and 23:56:32Z: 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 23:55:54.877Z and the first 'Charge request received.' at 23:56:32.929Z; every served charge after that logs 'Transaction complete.', and no failure/error lines were matched in payment's retained logs.

Events in otel-demo record the payment rollout: Deployment payment 'Scaled up replica set payment-7b6bfb9fb4 from 0 to 1' at 23:54:40Z, Pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started 23:54:40-23:54:43Z, ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 SuccessfulDelete and Pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 'Killing - Stopping container payment' at 23:54:43Z.

Deployment payment is at revision 2 with pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:54:40Z and an unchanged container image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment (strategy RollingUpdate, replicas 1); Deployment flagd is also revision 2 but with restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:23:29Z.

ConfigMap flagd-config (otel-demo) key demo.flagd.json holds the switched-on setting paymentFailure with defaultVariant "100%" (variant "100%" = 1, description "Fail payment service charge requests n%", state ENABLED); paymentUnreachable and every other flag in the file have defaultVariant "off".

The failure propagated through frontend: frontend's spans POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder each show 74 STATUS_CODE_ERROR increases in the window ending 23:56:00Z and 44 in the window ending 23:57:00Z, then 0; frontend's non-error GET span volume stayed around 1030-1100 per minute throughout.

The payment service recorded no ERROR-status spans in the window: its error rate is 0 at every sampled 5-minute step from 23:34Z to 00:09Z, and payment contributed 0 error spans in the per-service error series.

After the burst, checkout logs show successful orders ('[PlaceOrder]' followed by 'payment went through', 'order placed', confirmation email, Kafka 'Successful to write message') from 23:57:17Z through 23:58:58Z, matching checkout's zero Charge-error increases after the window ending 23:57:00Z.

All otel-demo pods are Running and their containers ready with restartCount 0; the payment pod is the only otel-demo pod created inside the incident window (creationTimestamp 2026-11-17T23:54:40Z, podIP 100.96.5.94), while checkout-5dccddf8bb-c4dqt and frontend-675fd7b5c5-sn9gc were created 23:21:42Z and 23:21:40Z.

The switched-on setting paymentFailure="100%" in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config is the fault behind the payment-path failures, with the payment Deployment restart at 23:54:40Z (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, unchanged image, new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4) as its mechanism and the 23:56-23:57Z checkout Charge/PlaceOrder errors, frontend /api/checkout errors and frontend-proxy ingress/egress error spans as its consequences.

Alternatively the burst is explained by the payment Deployment rollout itself: the only payment replica was removed at 23:54:43Z and the replacement only began serving at 23:56:32Z, so checkout's charge calls failed for about two minutes; this matches the observed absence of payment charge spans, but the object that requested the kubectl rollout restart is not visible in the evidence.

The observed failure mode in payment is absence of service, not injected charge failures: payment emitted no ERROR-status span at any sampled step, logged 'Transaction complete.' for every charge it served after 23:56:32Z while paymentFailure reads "100%", and logged no charge requests at all during 23:54:43Z-23:56:32Z.

frontend-proxy error spans are not limited to the payment incident: isolated errors were already recorded from 23:32Z (up to 0.0333/s at 23:36-23:40Z, with a sampled 503 at 23:37:56Z caused by an egress span with no upstream response) and are still present at 00:10:00Z (0.0077/s), so the payment event explains the 23:56-23:57Z burst but not the whole alert condition.

Rejected: that frontend or frontend-proxy themselves were down or restarted during the burst - their pods were created at 23:21:40Z/23:21:42Z with restartCount 0 and frontend continued serving about 1030-1100 GET spans per minute during the failing minutes.

Review the change history (not available in this Run) for who/what applied kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:54:40Z to Deployment payment, and the timeline of the paymentFailure flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, to confirm whether the flag change and the restart were the same deliberate fault injection.

Because payment runs a single replica with a ~71 s gap between container start (23:54:43Z) and its gRPC server start (23:55:54Z), a rolling restart removes all payment capacity; consider startup/readiness hardening or a surge replica so restarts do not produce charge failures, and review the >0 error-rate threshold that lets isolated 503s keep this alert firing.

gaps: The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate is not present in the Prometheus rules queried (exact rule_name lookup returned nothing), so its PromQL expression, threshold and evaluation window are unknown; the alert's stated current value 0.0111/s is consistent with 1 error span per ~90 s but this is not confirmed.

The actor/reason for the kubectl rollout restart recorded on Deployment payment at 2026-11-17T23:54:40Z is unknown; the change-history integration is not available in this Run and no Kubernetes event names who applied it.

The declared fault of the switched-on setting was not observed directly: payment never returned a charge error (no ERROR-status payment spans, all served charges logged 'Transaction complete.'), so whether paymentFailure="100%" was in effect during 23:54-23:57Z could not be verified, and the ConfigMap was read at about 00:16Z, after the authorized window.

Trace-level detail of the 23:56-23:57Z burst is unavailable: Jaeger's newest returned spans end at 23:41:24Z and searches for frontend, checkout, payment and frontend-proxy error traces inside 23:50-00:02Z returned nothing, so the HTTP status codes and error messages of the burst spans are unknown.

kube-state-metrics and HTTP/RPC application series were not available in this Prometheus (queries for kube_*, http_server_*, app_* and rpc_* metric names returned no series), so replica/endpoint-level confirmation of an empty payment endpoint set and the payment application's own transaction counters could not be checked.
The cause of the isolated frontend-proxy 503s outside the payment incident (e.g. 23:32-23:41Z with egress http.status_code=0) is not established by the evidence.

Whether the new payment pod was Ready only at 23:56:32Z (readiness probe behaviour) versus merely slow to start its gRPC server is unknown; only application logs and container start times were available.
next_steps: Obtain the change history for Deployment payment (kubectl rollout restart at 2026-11-17T23:54:40Z) and for ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config to confirm the sequence of the paymentFailure change and the restart.
Confirm from the payment application which feature flag it evaluates for charge failures and query flagd (or its UI/metrics) for the effective value of paymentFailure during 23:50-00:05Z.

Inspect frontend-proxy (Envoy) access/error logs for 23:56-23:57Z to capture the exact HTTP status codes and upstream error reasons of the failing ingress requests, and for the earlier isolated 503s at 23:32-23:41Z.
Check whether payment's readiness probe or startup delay can be shortened, or add a surge replica, so a single-replica rolling restart does not remove all payment capacity.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
